Make a pixel-art 2x2 eye-gaze atlas using only the exact attached local reference grid. Keep four equal 64:35 cells in this order: LEFT OPEN, RIGHT OPEN / LEFT HALF, RIGHT HALF. No labels, gutters, border, margins, or changed framing.

Preserve this character's sad brow shape, hair, skin, eye spacing, narrow original aperture, and crisp native pixel clusters. Keep both irises compact and olive-brown/amber with small dark pupils and only a tiny warm glint. Keep the eye interiors shaded muted brown-gray like the source: no cream or white bands, no large sclera areas, no oversized pupils, no glossy white glints.

In LEFT OPEN, both pupils and irises look gently toward the viewer's left, moving together in the same canvas direction with the source-like convergence. In RIGHT OPEN, both move gently toward the viewer's right. Do not leave either eye centered or make them cross-eyed.

For each HALF cell, lower only the upper eyelid to cover most of the iris while leaving a narrow visible portion of the iris and dark pupil. Preserve the source lower eyelid, cheek skin, and pixels beneath the eye exactly; do not move, reshape, or recolor the cheek edge. Keep brows unchanged in all four cells. The half-lidded row must not repeat the open row.

Use crisp nearest-neighbor pixel art, no smoothing, blur, painterly blending, vector shapes, new highlights, or expression changes.
